hunt.justification: Adversaries like Static Tundra specialize in converting unmanaged edge devices into long-term persistence nodes. Because these devices cannot run EDR agents, hunting in the network fabric for exfiltration and rare management access is the primary method to detect them.

scenario.summary: Static Tundra (Russian FSB Center 16) targets end-of-life Cisco network devices by exploiting CVE-2018-0171 and SNMP misconfigurations to gain initial access. The group maintains multi-year persistence using the SYNful Knock firmware implant and local user creation, focusing on configuration theft via TFTP for long-term espionage against strategic sectors.

hunt.name: Network Infrastructure Persistence and Exfiltration
hunt.description: This hunt identifies post-exploitation activity on network infrastructure, focusing on 'Static Tundra' (Russian FSB) TTPs. It focuses on devices vulnerable to CVE-2018-0171 and targets three behavioral signatures in the network fabric: configuration theft via TFTP, unauthorized management access (Telnet/SNMP), and rare inbound traffic from external source IPs. The hunt is designed to detect persistence that survives reboots and bypasses standard endpoint visibility.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS targets, MIN(time) AS first_access, MAX(time) AS last_access FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{management_ports}}' || ',', ',' || CAST(dst_endpoint_port AS TEXT) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING targets <= 2 ORDER BY targets ASC

config.expected_signal: Source IPs connecting to only one or two devices. These represent targeted access rather than fleet-wide management.

config.objective: Determine if any host identified in the scoping steps (CVE-2018-0171 or internet-exposed) shows evidence of exfiltration (TFTP) or unauthorized management access from rare IPs.
config.description: Correlate vulnerability exposure with rare behavioral hits to confirm state-sponsored intrusion.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious for any host combining vulnerability with outbound TFTP or rare inbound management traffic.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Direct confirmed hits to isolation and uncertain cases to manual review.
Sever the actor's connection and remove persistence artefacts.
config.instructions: Isolate the identified host at the switch/fabric level. Collect the running-config and startup-config for forensic analysis. Remove any unauthorized 'username' entries or 'snmp-server community' strings. Disable the TFTP server if enabled via 'no tftp-server'. Apply the patch for CVE-2018-0171 or disable Smart Install.

config.description: Perform deep manual inspection of the configuration retrieved during the action step.
config.instructions: Review the device configuration for the following artefacts: 1. New 'username' entries with high privilege levels. 2. Rogue 'snmp-server community' strings like 'public', 'anonymous', or 'public-rw'. 3. The presence of 'tftp-server nvram:startup-config' in the running configuration. 4. Modifications to TACACS+ or ACL settings that bypass remote logging or central control.

config.description: Document findings and hand off vulnerable devices to the patching team.
config.instructions: Record that no persistence indicators were found. Ensure all devices identified in the scoping phase (vulnerable to CVE-2018-0171) are tracked for patching or replacement if end-of-life.
